<cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 31:18">Targ. Ex. XXXI, 18</cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Numbers 11:26">Targ. O. Num. XI, 26</cite> (Y. <he>כתוביא</he>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 88a:21">B. Kam. 88ᵃ</cite> bot. <he>כְּתַבְתִּינְהוּ לניכסי וכ׳</he> she willed her property to &c.
<cite ref="Gittin 20a:7">Gitt. 20ᵃ</cite> <he>איהי קא כָתְבָה ליה</he> she (the wife) had it written (at her expense).
<cite ref="Bava Batra 168b:8">B. Bath. 168ᵇ</cite> <he>ולִיכְתּוֹב לן מר וכ׳</he> write for us another document (copy) in addition to this; a. v. fr.—

Sabb. 115ᵇ היכא דכְתִיבֵי תרגום וכ׳ when the books are written in Chaldaic or any other tongue (than Hebrew); a. fr.—Esp. (in arguments on Biblical texts) כ׳ or כ׳ רחמנא the Lord has written, the text reads.
<cite ref="Pesachim 21b:5">Pes. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>טעמא דכ׳ רחמנא וכ׳</he> this is so because the text reads <he>לא יֵאָכֵל</he> (passive voice), but if it did not read so &c.
<cite ref="Pesachim 21b:8">Ib.</cite> <he>לִכְתּוֹב רחמנא וכ׳</he> it ought to read &c.

Ber. 3ᵇ א״ה לכתוב מהנשף וכ׳ if this were so (that נשף invariably means evening), it ought to read (I Sam. XXX, 17) מהנשף ועד הנשף; a. v. fr.—כְּתִיב it is written, it reads (used also in Hebr. diction). Ib. 13ᵇ דִּכְ׳ לדבר בם for it says (Deut. XI, 19) ‘to speak thereof’; ה״נ הא כ׳ ודברת בם here, too, (in the first part of the Sh’ma) it says (VI, 7), ‘and thou shalt speak thereof’!—
Meg. 10ᵇ כ׳ הכא ויהי … וכ׳ התם ויהי here (Lev. IX, 1) vayhi is used, and there (Gen. I, 5) vayhi is used.
<cite ref="Genesis 1:5">Ib.</cite> <he>והָכְ׳</he>, <he>והא כ׳</he> but does it not also read &c.?—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 1:5">Gen. R. s. 1</cite> <he>ומאי כ׳ אחריו</he> and what do we read after this?—<he>הדא הוא דכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00003"><he>דָּא</he> I</cite>.—
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 71a:19">Snh. 71ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>בעינן קרא כְּדִכְ׳</he> we must construe the Biblical text as it is written (literally, e.g. Mish.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 8:4">ib. VIII, 4</cite> as an interpretation of <cite ref="Deuteronomy 21:19">Deut. XXI, 19</cite>); a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 66a:4">B. Kam. 66ᵃ</cite> <he>שינוי קונה כְּתִיבָה ותנינא כ׳</he> that a change of form of a stolen object gives possession (compelling the thief to restore in value) is written (intimated in the Biblical text) and has been taught in the Mishnah.—V. <cite ref="K01357"><he>כְּתִיב</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Megillah 7a:5">Meg. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>דאיבעי איכתיב וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>מאי דבעי כתיב</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note; Rashi: <he>דאי בעי כתב</he>) that which was liked was written down &c.; a. fr.
